Mis-assigned: this is Ehlers' Super Passband filter (TASC Jul 2016), not the EMD band-pass. The copy sums 50 squared PB values but divides by 40 (Ehlers: 50), so its RMS bands are sqrt(50/40) = 1.118x too wide; it also zeroes PB until bar_index > Period1. Implemented as ehlers_super_passband.

ehlers_bandpass.notes: Recursion matches the HPotter copies bar for bar when they are given the same pi (tested with 3.14 and 3.1415 through the private kernel). Output is na until price[2] exists, as in the copies. The HPotter +1/-1 zone/trigger states are strategy rules left to the caller. Super Passband: ehlers_super_passband(close, 40, 60, 50); Ehlers' 50-bar RMS confirmed in the EasyLanguage quoted at https://forums.worden.com/default.aspx?g=posts&t=65337 (TASC Jul 2016 Traders' Tips: https://traders.com/Documentation/FEEDbk_docs/2016/07/TradersTips.html).

ehlers_dominant_cycle.reference: John Ehlers, 'Measuring Cycles' (1999, Word doc): https://c.mql5.com/forextsd/forum/59/ehlers_measuring_cycles.doc (I-Q IFM SideBar 1, Cosine IFM SideBar 2, both sum 51 bars); Ehlers, Rocket Science for Traders (2001) ch. 7 homodyne discriminator (TA-Lib HT_DCPERIOD); phase-accumulation 'original approach' also in ProRealCode's Market Mode Strategies Sinewave port https://www.prorealcode.com/prorealtime-indicators/john-ehlers-sinewave/

strategy_issues.issue: getHT: 'InstPeriod = nz(InstPeriod[1])' inside the if-block declares a new local instead of assigning (':='), so on bars without a 360-degree crossing in 51 bars InstPeriod stays 0 and Period decays toward 0 instead of holding the last measurement. Fixed in ehlers_hilbert_period (tested on a 20-bar cycle that turns into a 120-bar one).

ehlers_dominant_cycle.notes: Four measurers. ehlers_iq_ifm matches the Fish Net getIQ (max 50, seed=1 for nz(lenIQ[1],1)) and Adaptive ZLEMA v2 (range 60) copies bar for bar from bar 0, and the Eltrut f_IQIFM copy after warm-up (it uses nz(src[7]) and nz(v1[4])). ehlers_cosine_ifm matches the Adaptive ZLEMA copies (range 50/100) from the first detected cycle on; before it the copies give na (inst := inst[1] without nz), Ehlers' code and ours give 0. Ehlers' own loops run 0..50; the copies use 50, 60, 100 or an input (max_count). ehlers_hilbert_period is the Fish Net getHT with the bug fixed (copy uses PI = 3.14159 in the degree conversion; ProRealCode's Sinewave sums 41 bars, Fish Net 51). ehlers_homodyne_dc (VAWSI copy, BlackCat1402's EhlersHoDyDC) equals TA-Lib HT_DCPERIOD to 1e-8 after warm-up and the VAWSI port. Ehlers' price is hl2 for the IFMs; the copies pass close. Fish Net's min clamp and VAWSI's ceil(1.1*p) in [1,34] are left to the caller.

ehlers_ec.notes: Matches the three Adaptive ZLEMA copies (62235ec98940, b0f1be861aa8) bar for bar, including least_error used in their threshold. ehlers_zero_lag_ec_adaptive takes a per-bar period series and reproduces the adaptive copies (round(Cosine IFM)) bar for bar, na periods included. Ehlers' defaults are Length 20, GainLimit 50; the copies use 8, 10, 15 or 50.

butterworth_2pole.reference: Ehlers, Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures (2004), 2-pole Butterworth: a = exp(-1.414*pi/P), b = 2a*cos(1.414*180/P), coef1 = (1-b+a^2)/4 on x + 2x[1] + x[2]; e.g. https://tw.tradingview.com/script/bD8PeDpX-Butterworth-2345poles-ATGS

strategy_issues.issue: butCMOmed mixes coefficient sets: cf21BW20/cf23BW20 with cf22BW50, so the filter is not a Butterworth of any length (wrong gain and response). Use ehlers_butterworth2(chandeMO, 20).

butterworth_2pole.notes: zero_seed=True reproduces the FMZ copies' nz() seeding bar for bar (variant_butt2pole in MA-Emperor-insiliconot and the two Moving-Average-Crossover strategies, and the cf21BW*/cf22BW*/cf23BW* lines of the Oscillating-Market-Long strategy, which uses pi = 3.14159265). Default follows Ehlers: first two bars = price, which removes the start-up transient. Copies and this function use exact sqrt(2); Ehlers prints 1.414.

ehlers_optimal_tracking.reference: Ehlers, Optimal Tracking Filter (Kalata tracking index); EasyLanguage-derived listing at https://www.prorealcode.com/prorealtime-indicators/john-ehlers-optimal-tracking-filter/ (Price = hl2, Value1 = .2*chg + .8*Value1[1], Value2 = .1*(H-L) + .8*Value2[1])
ehlers_optimal_tracking.notes: Variant, not a bug: the copies (f_kalman_filter) filter a moving average and smooth ta.tr instead of high-low; true_range=True reproduces them bar for bar. Default is Ehlers' H-L range. Zero-seeded like the EasyLanguage. When the smoothed range is exactly 0 the previous lambda is kept (Ehlers' 'If Value2 <> 0'); the copies would give na there. Original article not located online; formula cross-checked against the ProRealCode copy.

trendflex.reference: Ehlers, 'Reflex: A New Zero-Lag Indicator', TASC Feb 2020 (Traders' Tips https://traders.com/Documentation/FEEDbk_docs/2020/02/TradersTips.html; code as published at https://www.prorealcode.com/prorealtime-indicators/reflex-and-trendflex-indicators-john-f-ehlers/ : Super Smoother period .5*Length on (Close+Close[1])/2, MS = .04*Sum^2 + .96*MS[1])

strategy_issues.issue: Eltrut f_flex smooths with f_supersmoother(src, Length) - period Length instead of Ehlers' 0.5*Length and without the (src + src[1])/2 input average - so its Reflex/Trendflex is a different (slower) curve. The sum/MS loop itself is Ehlers' (tested through the private kernel).
Same Eltrut f_flex loop, fed by the period-Length smoother.

trendflex.notes: The TFO copy (380bfd896d56, a9fd45587b41) is Ehlers' Trendflex with its own parameters: ehlers_trendflex(close, 14, ss_length=8, ms_alpha=2/34) matches it after warm-up (it sums nz(superSmooth[i]) on the first bars). ss_length=0 means Ehlers' length/2. Uses exact sqrt(2) like both copies (Ehlers prints 1.414). Output is na for the first `length` bars; the copies print 0 there.

butterworth_3pole.reference: Ehlers, Cybernetic Analysis (2004) 3-pole Butterworth: a = exp(-pi/P), b = 2a*cos(1.738*180/P), c = a^2, coef1 = (1-b+c)(1-c)/8 (https://lavs9.github.io/quantwave/guides/indicators/native/butterworth3/); bilinear-transform Butterworth for the iirma copy
butterworth_3pole.notes: The iirma copy is not Ehlers' design but a correct bilinear-transform 3rd-order Butterworth with prewarping (coefficients checked by expanding H(s) = 1/(s^3+2s^2+2s+1)); method='bilinear' matches it bar for bar with exact pi and to 1e-6 with its 3.14159. Default method='ehlers'. Both seed the first 3 bars with the price, like the copy's nz(..., src).

ehlers_roofing_filter.reference: Ehlers, Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013) roofing filter; TASC Aug 2014 'The Quotient Transform' (Early Onset Trend, the Boom Hunter source: HP period 100, Super Smoother LPPeriod)
ehlers_roofing_filter.notes: Super Smoother stage c1*(HP + HP[1])/2 + c2*Filt[1] + c3*Filt[2] with 1.414 as in Ehlers and the copy. Identical to the Boom Hunter copy (hp 100, ss 6 and 28) after the start-up transient it inherits from its high-pass (nz(close[1]), see ehlers_highpass_2pole); bar for bar with Ehlers' code from bar 0. Ehlers' Cycle Analytics defaults hp 48, ss 10.

ehlers_cyber_cycle.reference: Ehlers, Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures (2004) ch. 4 Cyber Cycle (alpha .07, Price hl2, 'If CurrentBar < 7 then Cycle = (Price - 2*Price[1] + Price[2])/4')
ehlers_cyber_cycle.notes: Warm-up only: the copy tests na(cycle[7]), which keeps the start-up formula until bar 8 (Ehlers: bar 5). Identical after warm-up. signal = the strategy's EMA with alpha 1/(lag+1) (default lag 9); trigger = cycle[1] (Ehlers).

ehlers_smoothed_rsi.reference: Ehlers, Smoothed RSI (Rocket Science for Traders, 2001): CU/(CU+CD) over Length changes of (C + 2C[1] + 2C[2] + C[3])/6; HPotter port 'Smoothed RSI'
ehlers_smoothed_rsi.notes: Identical to HPotter's copies (3 files) from bar 3+Length on. Before that HPotter's iff() turns na comparisons into 0s and prints values from bar Length-1; this returns na. A window with no movement keeps the previous value (Ehlers); HPotter prints 0. The TopBand/LowBand position state is a strategy rule. Book listing not located online; formula as in HPotter's port, which credits Ehlers.

ehlers_highpass_2pole.reference: Ehlers, Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013) 2-pole high-pass: alpha1 = (cos(.707*360/P) + sin(.707*360/P) - 1)/cos(.707*360/P)

voss_filter.reference: Ehlers, 'A Peek Into The Future', TASC Aug 2019 (Traders' Tips https://www.traders.com/Documentation/FEEDbk_docs/2019/08/TradersTips.html): Period 20, Predict 3, Bandwidth .25

emdi_hpotter.reference: William Blau, Momentum, Direction and Divergence (1995): Ergodic Mean Deviation Indicator; HPotter 'Ergodic MDI' port

strategy_issues.issue: Minor: the SmthLen input is never used; the signal line is ema(ergodic, u). signal_length defaults to u (5) to match.

emdi_hpotter.notes: Mis-assigned to the Ehlers family: this is Blau's indicator (HPotter's comment says so). ema(ema(close - ema(close, r), s), u) with ta.ema seeding; pos = 1/-1 on ergodic above/below signal. Bar for bar with the copy.

ehlers_agc.reference: Ehlers, 'The Quotient Transform', TASC Aug 2014 (fast attack - slow decay AGC, decay .991); Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013)
ehlers_agc.notes: Peak = max(|x|, .991*Peak[1]); normalized = x/Peak. Bar for bar with the Boom Hunter copy (except it prints 0 instead of na while its input is na). Feed it ehlers_roofing_filter; the Quotient step (X+K)/(K*X+1) is one line left to the caller.

ehlers_decycler.reference: Ehlers, Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013) ch. 4 Decycler: Decycle = (alpha1/2)*(Close + Close[1]) + (1 - alpha1)*Decycle[1], alpha1 = (cos(360/P) + sin(360/P) - 1)/cos(360/P); see https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/decycler/
ehlers_decycler.notes: Bar for bar with the copy (nz seeding as written there). Default cutoff 60. TASC Sep 2015's 'Simple Decycler' (close minus a 2-pole high-pass, 125) is close - ehlers_highpass2(close, 125).

ehlers_fisher_stoch.reference: Ehlers, Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures (2004): Fisher transform of stochasticised indicators (Fisher Stochastic RVI / CG / Cyber Cycle): (4,3,2,1)/10 WMA of the stochastic, .5*ln((1+1.98(v-.5))/(1-1.98(v-.5)))
ehlers_fisher_stoch.notes: Generic: apply to any series (the strategy feeds its RVI). normalize=True divides by 2.64 as the copy does (a rescale, not Ehlers'). Bar for bar with the copy once its RVI warm-up has passed. On a flat stochastic window Ehlers keeps the previous value; Pine's stoch gives na there.

deli.reference: HPotter 'D_ELI' (Detrended Ehlers Leading Indicator), citing Ehlers, MESA and Trading Market Cycles, pp. 64-70 (DSP and Ehlers Leading Indicator)
deli.notes: HPotter's definition is the only one in use: DSP = ema(hl2, n) - ema(hl2, 2n), DELI = DSP - ema(DSP, n), pos = sign state (default n = 7). Bar for bar on the input series. The copy reads daily hl2 through security(); pass a daily series resampled without look-ahead yourself. HPotter's comment describes DSP as 2-pole minus 3-pole Butterworth, but his code (and this) uses EMAs.
